Team —

Draft plan below (sending early for internal alignment; I'll clean up for Arcadia):

1) Regression strategy overview (short):
- Baseline: we snapshot the serving model + evaluation artifacts at the time of contract signature. Baseline metrics include per-route latency, token-level perplexity, task-specific precision/recall on the supplied clinical extraction ground truth, and hallucination rate on the golden prompt set.
- Continuous monitoring: production telemetry collects sampled outputs (0.5–2% sampling depending on route) with automated scoring pipelines.
- Canary & holdout: new model variants are deployed to a canary cohort (1–5% traffic). We run parallel offline regression tests on a frozen holdout dataset derived from baseline + curated edge cases.
- Rollback triggers: automatic rollback on any of: 5%+ relative drop in task F1 on holdout, 10%+ increase in hallucination rate, or latency regression exceeding SLA threshold by 30%.
- Human-in-the-loop: for high-risk routes (clinical extraction) an analyst review gate is required before a global rollout.

2) Auditability & evidence:
- All model changes are versioned, with immutable release notes and hashes. We store model binaries and serving config in a retention bucket (customer-scoped retention policy).
- Evaluation artifacts (test inputs, seed, scoring scripts) are archived and accessible via signed links for the contract period.

3) Sample selection & transparency:
- Holdout is a mix of synthetic edge cases, anonymized historical examples (if permitted), and curated clinical testcases. We can accept Arcadia-supplied ground truth as an override for acceptance criteria.

Attachments I will prepare: regression-plan-outline.pdf and a short CSV describing holdout construction.

Questions for procurement: what retention window for logs/evidence do you require? 12/24/36 months?

- Rishi
Lead, Model Reliability
Redwood Inference
